title: COS 101 ( UNIZIK ) : COMPUTER HARDWARES AND SOFTWARE
subject: COS 101

questions.question: The system unit is made up of several components like which of the following?
questions.explanation: The system unit includes the motherboard, processor, buses, memory, and power supply unit.

questions.question: The CPU is considered the computer's most important single item because it performs which function?
questions.explanation: The microprocessor, or CPU, does all the PC's thinking and runs the programs requested by the user.

questions.question: The power supply unit converts high voltage electrical current to which type of voltage?
questions.explanation: The power supply unit converts high voltage electrical current to a low voltage to prevent components from blowing up.

questions.question: Which storage unit holds data permanently and is not affected when the PC is turned off?
questions.explanation: The hard disk is the computer's main permanent storage unit, holding large amounts of data and programs.

questions.question: The motherboard is made of a piece of fiberglass because fiberglass has which property?
questions.explanation: Fiberglass cannot conduct electricity, so each component is insulated from all others.

questions.question: CPU speed is measured in which unit?
questions.explanation: The speed of a CPU is measured in megahertz (MHz), which equals one million ticks per second.

questions.question: A computer keyboard is considered intelligent if it can do which of the following?
questions.explanation: An intelligent keyboard can initiate a series of actions for the computer to carry out by pressing a key.

questions.question: The intelligent computer keyboard has four major divisions, which include function keys, alphanumeric keys, numeric keys, and which other keys?
questions.explanation: The intelligent keyboard divisions are function keys, alphanumeric keys, numeric keys, and control keys.

questions.question: A general purpose keyboard most commonly contains how many keys?
questions.explanation: Most popular general purpose keyboards contain 101 keys.

questions.question: Which part of the keyboard contains alphabets, numbers, and special signs?
questions.explanation: The centered part of the keyboard known as the alphanumeric keypad contains alphabets, numbers, and special signs.

questions.question: Which part of the keyboard is mainly used for fast data entry in mathematical applications?
questions.explanation: The numeric keypad contains 0 to 9 numbers and mathematical signs used for fast data entry.

questions.question: Which keys are referred to as cursor-control or cursor-movement keys?
questions.explanation: Arrow keys are a set of four keys up, down, left, and right used to move the cursor on the screen.

questions.question: The first line of the keyboard contains a set of 12 keys named F1 to F12, which are known as?
questions.explanation: The first line of the keyboard contains a set of 12 keys with names F1 to F12 known as function keys.

questions.question: An ATM used in banks is an example of which type of keyboard application?
questions.explanation: Special purpose keyboards are used for special applications requiring faster data entry, like ATMs.

questions.question: A mouse consists of a pointing device, a roller ball, and a set of what?
questions.explanation: A mouse has a roller ball and two or more buttons which can be pressed to make a selection.

questions.question: Which printer type combines a magnetic roller with powdered ink called toner?
questions.explanation: Laser printers combine a magnetic roller with powdered ink called toner to transfer characters onto a page.

questions.question: Which printer type uses small nozzles to spray fast-drying ink onto a page?
questions.explanation: Inkjet printers spray a fine, quick-drying ink through small nozzles to produce characters and images.

questions.question: Which printer type is the cheapest available and creates characters out of a series of dots?
questions.explanation: Dot-matrix printers are the cheapest printers available and create characters by hammering pins against an inked ribbon.

questions.question: Which two monitor sizes are the most common?
questions.explanation: The two most common monitor sizes are 15-inch and 17-inch.

questions.question: VGA monitors have a resolution of which dimensions?
questions.explanation: VGA is 640x480 (width by height).

questions.question: Which scanner type looks and behaves a lot like a photocopier?
questions.explanation: Flatbed scanners look and behave a lot like a photocopier.

questions.question: Which scanner type is a low-cost alternative that is moved manually over a flat surface?
questions.explanation: Hand scanners are manual devices you move over a flat surface, just like a PC's mouse.

questions.question: A subwoofer is designed to improve which type of sound?
questions.explanation: A subwoofer improves the bass (low notes) sound.

questions.question: Computer software is divided into which two major groups?
questions.explanation: Computer software is divided into system software and application software.

questions.question: System software provides a suitable environment for which activity?
questions.explanation: System software facilitates the writing, editing, debugging, testing, and running of user programs.

questions.question: An operating system acts as an interface between which two entities?
questions.explanation: An operating system is a program that acts as an interface between a user of a computer and the computer hardware.

questions.question: Which type of operating system collects jobs into a batch with no user interaction during processing?
questions.explanation: In a batch processing environment, users submit jobs to a central place where they are collected into a batch.

questions.question: Which operating system provides computing services to several users concurrently online?
questions.explanation: Time-sharing operating systems provide computing services to several users concurrently online.

questions.question: Which operating system is designed to service applications where response time is of the essence?
questions.explanation: Real-time operating systems are designed to service those applications where response time is of the essence.

questions.question: A multiprogramming operating system allows more than one active user program to be stored where?
questions.explanation: A multiprogramming operating system allows more than one active user program to be stored in main memory simultaneously.

questions.question: A multiprocessing system is a computer hardware configuration that includes which feature?
questions.explanation: A multiprocessing system is a computer hardware configuration that includes more than one independent processing unit.

questions.question: A distributed operating system appears to its users as which type of system?
questions.explanation: A distributed operating system appears to its users as a traditional uniprocessor system, even though it is composed of multiple processors.

questions.question: Which operating system component is responsible for keeping track of which parts of memory are currently being used and by whom?
questions.explanation: The operating system's memory management component keeps track of which parts of memory are currently being used and by whom.

questions.question: Which operating system component is responsible for disk scheduling?
questions.explanation: Secondary storage management handles disk scheduling, free space management, and storage allocation.

questions.question: In the I/O system, which component knows the peculiarities of a specific hardware device?
questions.explanation: Only the device driver knows the peculiarities of a specific device.

questions.question: A file is defined as a collection of related information that is defined by its creator and is a sequence of what?
questions.explanation: A file is a sequence of bits, bytes, lines, or records whose meaning is defined by its creator and user.

questions.question: The command interpreter is also known by which name in UNIX?
questions.explanation: The command interpreter is variously called the control card interpreter, command line interpreter, or shell (in UNIX).

questions.question: Utility software performs operations such as file conversion, file copy, and which other type?
questions.explanation: Utility software performs operations like file conversion, file copy, and housekeeping operations.

questions.question: Application software designed to solve problems of a specific nature can be subdivided into which two classes?
questions.explanation: Application software is subdivided into generalized software and user-defined software.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a communication package?
questions.explanation: Communication packages include Carbon Plus, Data Talk V3.3, Cross Talk, SAGE Chit Chat, and Data Soft.

questions.question: A payroll package developed for the salary operation of a particular company is an example of which type of software?
questions.explanation: User programs are a suite of programs written by programmers for computer users to operate their individual business or tasks.

questions.question: Humanware is the combination of hardware and software elements that makes which interaction as good as possible?
questions.explanation: Humanware makes human interaction with a device as good as possible.

questions.question: The ability to navigate, understand, and utilize digital technologies effectively is known as which term?
questions.explanation: Digital literacy is the ability to navigate, understand, and utilize digital technologies effectively.

questions.question: Designing interfaces and interactions that are intuitive, efficient, and enjoyable for users is known as which term?
questions.explanation: UX design involves designing interfaces and interactions that are intuitive, efficient, and enjoyable for users.

questions.question: Understanding and following social norms and expectations when using digital technologies is known as which term?
questions.explanation: Digital etiquette involves understanding and following social norms and expectations when using digital technologies.

questions.question: Ensuring that technology can be used by people with diverse abilities and backgrounds is known as which term?
questions.explanation: Accessibility and inclusion is ensuring that technology can be used by people with diverse abilities and backgrounds.

questions.question: Which of the following is an application of computers in the field of education?
questions.explanation: Information processing in education includes personalized learning through learning management systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is an application of computers in healthcare?
questions.explanation: Computer applications in healthcare include telemedicine for remote consultations and diagnosis.

questions.question: Which of the following is an application of computers in the military?
questions.explanation: Autonomous vehicles and drones are among the applications of computers in the military and transportation sectors.

questions.question: Which of the following is an application of computers in banking?
questions.explanation: Computer applications in banking include creating secure online banking systems.
